grh_65755659a9f02943210e.title: Christmas Deferred
paragraphs: Six-year-old Ted Ward was gravely ill and unconscious through the previous Christmas, and his mother Ruth has never told him that the holiday passed while he slept. Ruth has also cut herself and Ted off from Rivers End, embittered by the disgrace and death of her husband Glenn after he took money from a bank and, she believes, was never given a chance to make restitution. When Dr. Christian learns that Ted is waiting for a Christmas he thinks is still ahead, he and newspaper editor Matt Redding decide to give it to him in midsummer. Matt publishes Ted's story and August 8 becomes a community Christmas, drawing gifts, letters, a tree and old neighbors who rediscover their own generosity. Christian deliberately shows Ruth how the project is healing other wounded people too, including an elderly craftsman who resumes making toys after losing his son in the war and former enemies who reconcile while baking Christmas cookies. Ruth's resistance finally breaks as she sees Ted brighten and the town answer bitterness with kindness. When Ted's grandmother tries to remove him from the excitement, Ted insists the celebration is helping him. Afterward he admits to Christian that he eventually realized it was August, not December, but continued the make-believe because the unusual Christmas was doing as much good for his mother and grandmother as it was for him.

grh_655cc166ee139f9ba2f6.title: Lifeboat
paragraphs: Survivors of a ship torpedoed in the Atlantic crowd into a lifeboat, joined by Willi, a German from the U-boat that sank them. The Americans and Britons argue over whether to trust him, but gradually surrender navigation and survival decisions to the calm, capable sailor. They discover too late that Willi has hidden water and supplies, deceived them about their course and is steering them toward a German vessel; after the injured Gus dies and Willi's betrayal becomes undeniable, the survivors turn on and kill him. Forced to row and think for themselves, they are finally spotted during a naval battle and expect rescue. When another young German sailor climbs aboard with a gun, they disarm rather than kill him, ending with the unresolved question of what war requires people to become.

grh_653b4dbb69b3807809f8.title: The Visit
paragraphs: Peter Ratner and his wife Laurie use a European trip as cover for a dangerous visit to Zantburg, where Peter's mother has remained since she sacrificed her own escape years earlier so her husband could flee with their infant son. Peter finds her and plans to take her to the West, but the local chief constable becomes suspicious of the American couple, arrests them, dismantles their van and tries to force them to identify a supposed local traitor. Peter's mother intervenes, helps them escape custody and joins their flight across the countryside. Evading searchers, the three find a concealed route leading across the border, where an ally has prepared new papers, money and tickets home. The rescue succeeds because strangers and family members alike decide that having the ability to help also creates a reason to act.

grh_65e8a8d851eaee45263d.title: The Man with the Twisted Lip
paragraphs: Watson's search for a friend's missing husband leads him to an opium den, where Holmes is investigating the disappearance of Neville Sinclair. Witnesses saw Sinclair at an upstairs window before the disfigured beggar Hugh Boone was arrested, and clothing and blood make murder seem likely. Holmes finally realizes that Boone and Sinclair are the same man. Sinclair had once discovered that begging in disguise earned far more than respectable work and secretly maintained the double life to support his family. Caught changing identities, he tried to conceal the truth rather than face his wife and children. With no murder committed, Holmes secures his release on the condition that the beggar persona disappears forever.

grh_658b8b726fe9b07f7e8d.title: Turnabout Is Foul Play
paragraphs: In Bern, Harry overhears German industrialist Hans Croft and a fixer discussing plans to obtain confidential Western European reconstruction information. Harry joins a counter-scheme involving official Bill Foster, who supplies convincing but false plans. Croft entrusts £30,000 to Harry during the deal, and Harry prepares matching envelopes so he can secretly keep the cash. Croft's daughter Frieda, who has fallen for Harry, learns the truth and insists the tainted money should go to a refugee organization. Harry switches the envelopes on her, but Frieda notices and switches them back. From his departing train Harry reads her note explaining that she loves him but cannot become the wife of another criminal, while the full £30,000 goes to the refugees.

grh_65b63bcff6afee61c5b3.title: Double Double Cross
paragraphs: Harry falls for Louise and agrees to work with her and Pierre as an airborne courier, parachuting packages between France and England for a thousand pounds a trip. On a later run, Pierre pushes Harry from the plane while Louise has anonymously tipped Scotland Yard that Harry will be landing with a large amount of illegal currency. Police are indeed waiting, but their search finds that every carefully sealed packet contains only brown paper. Louise and Pierre had also replaced the money in an effort to cheat Harry, so their two betrayals cancel each other out and leave him with nothing incriminating. Harry walks free and concludes that war is less dangerous than romance.

grh_6514377f2de7053c82ba.title: Danny Gets Married
paragraphs: At Christmas, Dr. Christian watches nurse Goldie devote herself to Tony, a seriously ill boy in the Center City hospital, while young Dr. Danny Bradford quietly falls in love with her. Tony worries about what will happen to Goldie when he is no longer there for her and decides that Bradford is the man who ought to look after her. The adults hesitate to say openly what they feel, but Tony finally forces the question at the child's Christmas celebration, asking Goldie whether she wants Bradford as her Christmas present. She admits that she does. Dr. Christian later explains that Danny Bradford and Goldie were married the following Christmas Day, with Tony recovering slowly but steadily.
